authority: AAU curriculum-owned assessment inputs. The agent must not invent replacement problems when an exercise pack is supplied.
evidence_rule: Inline exercise data are training-case inputs, not claims about the external world. Cite them as CURRICULUM_CASE_DATA. External research is forbidden unless external_research=true.

QDA601-M1-U1.title: Ratios and Rates
problems: Funnel: 1,260 leads produced 189 trials and 54 paid customers. Calculate lead→trial, trial→paid, and lead→paid rates; state units and reverse-check the implied counts.
Pricing/KPI: price rises from $80 to $92 while gross-margin rate rises from 40% to 46%. Distinguish percentage change from percentage-point change for both measures.
Defects: 36 defects occur in 120,000 transactions. Express the defect rate per 1,000 and per 10,000; at the same rate estimate defects for 185,000 transactions and reverse-check.
Growth/churn: revenue rises from $2.40m to $2.76m while monthly churn falls from 4.5% to 3.6%. Report relative percentage changes and percentage-point change where appropriate.

QDA601-M1-U2.title: Algebra for Decisions
problems: Profit equation: monthly profit = P·Q − 18Q − 72,000. If Q=6,000 and target profit is $30,000, solve for P and verify by substitution.
Break-even: price=$65, variable cost=$29, fixed cost=$126,000. Solve break-even volume; then solve required volume for $54,000 operating profit.
LTV/CAC: LTV = monthly gross profit per customer / monthly churn. Monthly gross profit=$42 and churn=3.5%. Solve LTV, then maximum CAC for an LTV:CAC target of 3.2×.

QDA601-M1-U3.title: Growth and Discounting
problems: Compound $2.40m revenue at 18% annually for 3 years; independently reverse using a logarithmic/ratio check.
Monthly logo retention is 96.5%. Compute 12-month retention and annualized churn implied by compounding; contrast with simply multiplying monthly churn by 12.
Discount cash receipts of $140k, $175k, and $210k at years 1–3 using an 11% annual discount rate; state PV and verify by re-compounding each PV.

QDA601-M1-U4.title: Dimensional Sanity
problems: Audit this model: 8,500 monthly orders × $42/order × 12 = $4.284m annual revenue; marketing cost is recorded as 310 (labeled '$000 per month'); CAC is shown as $31 when 1,250 customers are acquired monthly. Identify every unit/scale inconsistency and correct it.
A plant reports energy use 2.4 kWh/unit and 180,000 units/month but multiplies by an electricity price of 14 cents/kWh as if it were $14. Recompute monthly energy cost and quantify the scale error.
Sanity-check a claim that a $6m market supports $15m annual revenue at 12% share. Identify the contradiction and the implied market size needed.

QDA601-M2-U1.title: Time Value of Money
problems: Compute NPV of an initial $300k outflow followed by $95k, $120k, $145k, and $165k at years 1–4 using a 10% discount rate.
Compute future value of $180k invested for 30 months at 8% nominal annual interest compounded monthly.
A contract pays $24k at each year-end for 6 years. Compute PV at 9% and independently verify using explicit discounted cash flows rather than only the annuity formula.

QDA601-M2-U2.title: Unit Economics
problems: Channel A: spend $84k, 1,200 acquired customers, monthly ARPU $48, gross margin 72%, monthly churn 4%. Compute CAC, monthly gross profit/customer, simple steady-state LTV, LTV:CAC, and CAC payback months.

Channel B: spend $60k, 600 acquired customers, ARPU $72, gross margin 78%, monthly churn 2.8%. Compute the same metrics and compare with A without treating the simple LTV formula as a cohort observation.
Stress both channels at churn +1.2 percentage points and gross margin −5 percentage points. State which conclusion changes, if any.

QDA601-M2-U3.title: Cash Survival
problems: Opening cash=$420k; monthly fixed cash opex=$105k; sales=3,000 units/month; price=$68; variable cash cost=$31/unit; cash collections occur one month after sale. Model six months of cash assuming month 1 begins with no receivables.
Downside: volume falls 20%, variable cost rises 10%, and collections slip to two months. Recompute runway.
Find the monthly volume required for operating cash break-even under the base case and under the downside variable cost.

QDA601-M2-U4.title: Valuation and Thresholds
problems: Project costs $500k now and produces annual cash flows of $150k, $185k, $210k, $225k for years 1–4. Compute NPV at 12%.
Holding years 1–3 fixed, solve the minimum year-4 cash flow for NPV=0.
A product has contribution margin $24/order, annual fixed incremental cost $360k, and launch cost $180k. Find first-year order volume needed to recover both fixed and launch costs.

QDA601-M3-U1.title: Conditional Probability
problems: A fraud detector has sensitivity 92%, specificity 96%, and fraud prevalence 1.5%. For 100,000 transactions, build the confusion matrix and compute P(fraud|flagged).
Supplier A provides 60% of components with 1% defect rate; B provides 40% with 3% defect rate. Compute P(B|defective).
State which quantities are joint, marginal, and conditional; test whether supplier and defect status are independent.

QDA601-M3-U2.title: Expectation and Variance
problems: Project A payoff: −$120k (0.20), $80k (0.50), $300k (0.30). Project B: −$20k (0.35), $110k (0.40), $210k (0.25). Compute expected payoff and variance/standard deviation.
Compare downside probability and expected shortfall below zero for both projects.
Explain why equal or similar expected values would not imply equal decisions when liquidity loss tolerance is $100k.

QDA601-M3-U3.title: Bayesian Updating
problems: Prior probability that true high demand exists is 0.30. A positive pilot result has P(+|high)=0.80 and P(+|low)=0.25. Compute posterior after a positive pilot.
A second independent signal conditional on demand has P(+|high)=0.70 and P(+|low)=0.35. Update again after a second positive signal.
Then update the first posterior for a negative second signal and compare how strongly the evidence should change the thesis.

QDA601-M3-U4.title: Decision Trees
problems: Launch now costs $400k. If demand is high (0.45), net payoff after cost is +$900k; if low, −$300k. Delay for a $70k test: test is positive with probability 0.55; after positive, P(high)=0.75, after negative P(high)=0.18. After testing you may launch or kill. Build the optimal decision tree.
Compute expected value of launch-now, test-then-decide, and kill-now.
State the value of the test before cost and after cost; verify no branch double-counts sunk test cost.

QDA601-M4-U1.title: Distributions and Descriptives
problems: For the supplied store conversion-time dataset (minutes), compute mean, median, Q1, Q3, IQR, and identify outliers using 1.5×IQR.
Compare the mean with and without the largest observation and explain aggregation risk.
Segment the first six vs last six observations and show how a single overall mean can hide heterogeneity.

QDA601-M4-U2.title: Sampling and Confidence
problems: Campaign A converts 420 of 6,000 visitors; B converts 500 of 6,250. Compute rates and approximate 95% confidence intervals for each proportion.
Compute an approximate 95% CI for the difference B−A and state whether zero is included.
A retention sample observes 342 retained of 400 users. Estimate the proportion and 95% CI; explain what the interval does and does not claim.

QDA601-M4-U3.title: Regression and Association
problems: Interpret each coefficient with units and ceteris-paribus language.
Approximate t-statistics for coefficients and discuss statistical evidence without converting association into causation.
Explain why the pairwise ad-spend correlation and multivariable coefficient answer different questions; identify plausible confounders.

QDA601-M4-U4.title: Messy Data Lab
problems: Define a deterministic cleaning pipeline: types, dates, currency, duplicate handling, missing revenue, region normalization, and outlier review.
Do not silently convert EUR to USD without a supplied FX rate; classify the unresolved value and show which aggregates can/cannot be computed.
Identify likely scale errors and produce a cleaned-record ledger with every transformation documented.

QDA601-M5-U1.title: Causal Claims

case_data.observed: Users who enabled feature X had 18% higher 30-day retention.
case_data.selection: Feature X was optional and adopters had 2.1x prior-week sessions before enabling.

problems: Separate the descriptive association from any causal claim.
Identify at least three alternative explanations/confounders.
State the strongest conclusion supported and design evidence that would move the claim toward causality.

QDA601-M5-U2.title: Bias and Confounding

case_data.cohort_rule: Only customers active at both start and end of year were included
case_data.measurement_change: Revenue definition began including service fees midyear

problems: Identify survivorship, selection, and measurement biases.
Explain direction of likely bias where possible and where direction is unknown.
Specify a corrected cohort/measurement design and the minimum data needed.

QDA601-M5-U3.title: Evidence States
claims: Q2 revenue was $4.2m according to audited ledger.
Price elasticity is −1.4 based on a fitted historical model.
We assume 3% monthly churn in the base case.
Calculated CAC is $84 from $420k spend / 5,000 new customers.
Customers value faster onboarding because interview notes repeatedly mention setup time.
problems: Label each claim OBSERVED, CALCULATED, ESTIMATED, ASSUMED, INFERRED, or FORECAST and justify.
Identify which labels require source provenance versus formula provenance.
Rewrite the six claims into a traceable evidence-state ledger.

QDA601-M5-U4.title: Experiment Design
problems: State hypothesis, null, treatment, control, primary metric, guardrails, and stopping criteria.
Translate the 15% relative lift into an absolute conversion target.
Describe randomization and contamination risks; define a kill criterion that can falsify the demand thesis.

QDA601-M6-U1.title: Demand and Elasticity
problems: At price $50 demand is 12,000 units; at $55 demand is 10,900. Compute midpoint price elasticity and revenue at both prices.
Using elasticities −0.6, −1.0, and −1.8 around a $60 price with 20,000 baseline units, estimate directional revenue response to a 10% price increase using the elasticity approximation.
State limitations of extrapolating constant elasticity.

QDA601-M6-U2.title: Marginal Economics
problems: Compute incremental monthly profit for each capacity option at expected extra demand, respecting capacity limits.
Find the extra-demand threshold where B becomes preferable to A.
State the opportunity cost of choosing insufficient capacity if actual extra demand is 6,000.

QDA601-M6-U3.title: Market Structure
problems: Compute HHI from supplied shares and interpret concentration descriptively.
Assess supplier power, buyer power, entry barriers, and substitution using only supplied evidence.
Build a quantified entrant risk ledger; distinguish observed case data from inferred strategic implications.

QDA601-M6-U4.title: Incentives and Strategic Response
problems: Compute contribution profit for each supplied scenario.
Explain how competitor response changes the optimal pricing conclusion.
Identify incentive compatibility concerns for a reseller paid 12% of revenue versus 20% of gross profit.

QDA601-M7-U1.title: Sensitivity Analysis
problems: Compute base contribution after fixed cost and acquisition spend.
One-at-a-time sensitivities: price ±10%, volume ±20%, variable cost ±15%, CAC ±25%. Quantify output change and rank variables by absolute effect.
Explain why one-at-a-time sensitivity can miss interactions.

QDA601-M7-U2.title: Scenario Modeling
problems: Compute monthly operating contribution for each linked scenario.
Explain why scenario variables should be coherent rather than independently cherry-picked.
Add cash runway using opening cash $900k and treat negative contribution as burn; state limitations if working capital is omitted.

QDA601-M7-U3.title: Threshold and Reversal Analysis
problems: Solve break-even volume before acquisition spend and after acquisition spend.
Holding other inputs fixed, solve maximum CAC for monthly operating contribution >= $100k.
Using simple LTV=(price−variable_cost)/churn, solve the churn rate at which LTV:CAC falls below 3×.

QDA601-M7-U4.title: Value of Information
problems: Compute expected value without additional information.
For each test, use Bayes to determine posterior after positive/negative outcomes and optimal follow-up decision.
Compute expected value of sample information net of test cost and choose the next experiment based on decision value.

QDA601-M8-U1.title: Canonical Variable Ledger
problems: Create a canonical ledger with variable, value, unit, period, evidence state, source, and confidence.
Do not average contradictions. State the authority/reconciliation rule used for each canonical value or leave unresolved.
List every unresolved definition needed before downstream modeling.

QDA601-M8-U2.title: Contradiction Detection
statements: Finance: gross margin=76% excluding support payroll.
Ops: gross margin=68% including support payroll.
problems: Identify value conflicts versus definition/period conflicts.
Normalize periods where mathematically valid without pretending definitions are equivalent.
Produce a contradiction ledger and name the controlling definition required for each downstream decision.

QDA601-M8-U3.title: Dependency Propagation
problems: Compute monthly gross profit, simple LTV, LTV:CAC, and CAC payback months.
Change canonical churn from 3% to 4.5%. Recompute every dependent output and enumerate dependencies changed.
Change gross margin from 75% to 68% as a second perturbation and reconcile all downstream metrics.

QDA601-M8-U4.title: Reconciliation Defense
problems: Choose or leave unresolved each canonical value using source authority and definitions, never averaging.
Defend each choice against an adversarial challenge that the higher/lower number is more favorable.
State how unresolved variables should propagate as ranges/UNKNOWN rather than false precision.

QDA601-M9-U1.title: Reproducible Calculations
problems: State formulas independently, then compute contribution/customer, CAC, simple LTV, LTV:CAC, and payback.
Provide deterministic pseudocode or code-like steps that reproduce the values from named inputs.
Independently hand-reconstruct at least two outputs and compare with the computational result.

QDA601-M9-U2.title: Data Pipeline
problems: Specify an idempotent cleaning pipeline with schema, parsing, canonical IDs, date policy, duplicate rule, missing-value rule, and status normalization.
Produce expected cleaned rows under an explicitly stated date-format assumption; flag any ambiguous date rather than silently guessing.
Define aggregation checks that would catch duplicate revenue and invalid null/refund treatment.

QDA601-M9-U3.title: Simulation and Uncertainty
problems: Define monthly profit = volume*(price−variable_cost)−fixed_cost and a reproducible Monte Carlo procedure with a fixed seed and at least 10,000 draws.

Report which statistics must be produced: mean, median, P10, P90, probability(profit<0). If computation tooling is unavailable, do not invent simulated numbers; provide exact deterministic setup and bounded analytical checks instead.
Perform best/mode/worst corner sanity checks and explain why corners are not probability quantiles.

QDA601-M9-U4.title: Consistency Testing
problems: Design deterministic invariant tests and evaluate both supplied cases.
For every failure, identify the exact violated invariant and expected value/range.
Separate arithmetic consistency failures from plausible-but-unverified business assumptions.

QDA601-M10-U1.title: Raw Evidence Intake

sources.claim: 6,200 active paying accounts at Q2 end; ARPA $255/month
14 of 20 interviewees cite onboarding time as top pain

problems: Build an evidence ledger with state labels, scope, period, authority, and limitations.
Check whether billing snapshot metrics reconcile approximately with quarterly revenue; explain timing/recognition limitations rather than forcing equality.
Identify which claims can enter an integrated model as observations versus assumptions/forecasts.

QDA601-M10-U2.title: Integrated Model
problems: Build one canonical monthly model covering revenue, gross profit, simple LTV, LTV:CAC, acquisition spend, operating contribution, and runway direction.
Distinguish observed starting inputs from forecast assumptions and calculate a 12-month base case with clearly stated simplifying assumptions.
Run downside: growth/new accounts −25%, churn +1.5pp, gross margin −6pp, CAC +20%; identify decision-critical changes.

QDA601-M10-U3.title: Adversarial Audit
problems: Without trusting the first solution, reconstruct monthly revenue, gross profit, simple LTV=(ARPA*GM)/churn, and LTV:CAC from authoritative inputs.
Compare each reconstructed value to the frozen first solution; quantify any discrepancy and classify arithmetic vs definition issues.
Attack at least three assumptions behind simple LTV and state what evidence would be needed for a stronger cohort model.

QDA601-M10-U4.title: Decision and Perturbation Defense
problems: Compute base NPV and make BUILD/REVISE/KILL using the supplied $250k strategic NPV threshold; state that the threshold is a course rule, not universal truth.
Apply each perturbation independently and recompute the decision.
Apply all three perturbations jointly, identify the reversal driver(s), and defend the recommendation with explicit UNKNOWNs and kill/revisit criteria.
